included.title: Knowing When to Abstain: Medical LLMs Under Clinical Uncertainty
included.dal_implication: Explicit medical abstention, conformal prediction, and adversarial uncertainty evaluation are prior art; DAL must contribute beyond an abstain option.

included.title: LLMs (Almost) Never Abstain Under Medical Uncertainty
included.dal_implication: Missing-answer medical MCQA and overcommitment evaluation are established; Study 1 must test richer evidence insufficiency and action policies.

included.title: Large Language Models lack essential metacognition for reliable medical reasoning
included.dal_implication: Accuracy and knowing-when-not-to-answer must be evaluated separately.

included.title: Large language model uncertainty proxies: discrimination and calibration for medical diagnosis and treatment
included.dal_implication: Self-reported confidence is insufficient; Study 1 should compare multiple uncertainty signals and measure both discrimination and calibration.

included.title: Probabilistic medical predictions of large language models
included.dal_implication: Explicit confidence can be inferior to implicit probability signals, especially with smaller models and imbalanced datasets.

included.title: When silence is safer: a review and decision-theoretic framework for LLM abstention in healthcare
included.dal_implication: Decision-theoretic abstention is established prior work; DAL cannot claim this concept alone as novel.

included.title: Holistic evaluation of large language models for medical tasks with MedHELM
included.dal_implication: A definitive DAL study cannot rely on one exam-style QA dataset; evaluation should span complementary clinical task classes.

included.title: Testing and Evaluation of Health Care Applications of Large Language Models: A Systematic Review
included.dal_implication: Accuracy-dominant, exam-style evaluation is insufficient; real clinical data, broader metrics, bias and deployment considerations strengthen Study 1.

included.title: How to meaningfully evaluate AI in clinical medicine
included.dal_implication: Study claims must be bounded to what the evaluation setup truly measures; benchmark score alone is not application readiness.

included.title: General-purpose large language models outperform specialized clinical AI tools on medical benchmarks
included.dal_implication: Blinded clinician review of de-identified real clinical queries is a strong external-validation model, while public benchmarks remain contamination-prone.

included.title: Evaluating the robustness and readiness of large frontier models in health AI applications
included.dal_implication: Study 1 should include adversarial or information-removal stress tests and avoid equating high benchmark scores with robust reasoning.

included.title: Evaluation and mitigation of the limitations of large language models in clinical decision-making
included.dal_implication: Realistic clinical workflows expose failures hidden by licensing-exam QA; evidence order, missing information and guideline adherence matter.

included.title: AgentClinic: a multimodal benchmark for tool-using clinical AI agents
included.dal_implication: Static QA alone is insufficient for agentic clinical decision evaluation; sequential tool use is established benchmark territory.

included.title: FHIR-AgentBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Interoperable Electronic Health Records
included.dal_implication: FHIR-grounded agent evaluation is prior art; DAL must treat interoperability as an evaluation setting, not a novelty claim.

included.title: BRIDGE: benchmarking large language models for understanding real-world clinical practice texts
included.dal_implication: Real-world EHR-derived multilingual evaluation provides a stronger external-validity target than exam-style QA alone.

included.title: Answering real-world clinical questions using large language model, retrieval-augmented generation, and agentic systems
included.dal_implication: Evidence-grounded answers and physician-rated actionability are prior art; DAL should evaluate whether assurance changes justified action, not merely citation presence.

included.title: Reliability of LLMs as medical assistants for the general public: a randomized preregistered study
included.dal_implication: Strong model-only performance need not translate to human benefit; external user or clinician evaluation should be separated from benchmark performance.

included.title: TRIPOD+AI statement
included.dal_implication: Study 1 reporting should explicitly document data sources, model development, evaluation and limitations.

included.title: Medical Graph RAG: Evidence-based Medical Large Language Model via Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation
included.dal_implication: Evidence-grounded retrieval and credible sourcing are established; provenance alone is not sufficient DAL novelty.

included.title: Reporting guideline for the early-stage clinical evaluation of decision support systems driven by artificial intelligence: DECIDE-AI
included.dal_implication: Any later live or clinician-facing DAL evaluation should follow established early-stage clinical AI reporting principles.

included.title: A novel evaluation benchmark for medical LLMs illuminating safety and effectiveness in clinical domains
included.dal_implication: Safety and effectiveness require multidimensional, consequence-aware evaluation beyond accuracy and calibration alone.

included.title: Limited benchmarks constrain the conclusions of a general-purpose versus clinical AI comparison
included.dal_implication: Public-benchmark contamination, evaluator affinity, small real-world samples and underspecified inference settings can invalidate broad superiority claims.

not_novel: medical abstention or explicit abstain options
medical RAG or evidence provenance alone
novelty_gap_candidate.candidate: A risk-controlled, evidence-bound action policy that jointly measures strong medical QA utility, calibrated uncertainty, semantic evidence sufficiency and contradiction, abstain/escalate behavior, bounded revision, and auditable provenance under adversarial information insufficiency and realistic external evaluation.

protocol_implications: Select QA candidates with macro-F1 and balanced accuracy in addition to accuracy to prevent majority-class collapse.
Evaluate uncertainty discrimination and calibration separately; do not rely on verbalized confidence alone.
Construct evidence-insufficiency cases that cannot be solved by detecting context presence or absence.
Constrain target coverage by the answerable fraction and preregister deterministic tie handling.
Use a held-out calibration set for any risk-control threshold; final labels cannot tune thresholds.
Use multiple complementary evaluation settings rather than one public medical QA benchmark.
Include adversarial information removal or perturbation and realistic EHR/FHIR or agentic evaluation where licenses and compute permit.
Track benchmark contamination risk and treat previously inspected Study 0 rows as pilot-only evidence.
Keep model-only benchmark performance separate from clinician- or user-rated external utility.
Apply TRIPOD+AI and DECIDE-AI principles where applicable to reporting and later external evaluation.
limitations: This is a pre-protocol targeted refresh, not yet a PRISMA systematic review.
Scite MCP was unavailable under the zero-cost constraint because it required a paid plan or active trial.
ResearchRabbit, Connected Papers, Litmaps, Elicit, SciSpace, Zotero and Gemini Notebook were not treated as primary evidence authorities in this pass.
Citation chasing and benchmark licensing/contamination screening remain separate SG-000025 work before novelty freeze.
Preprints, if later included, must remain explicitly distinguished from peer-reviewed evidence.
